findings.title: False terminal coefficient in the exact energy representation
locators: Physical/printed21, Lemma9.1, equations(90),(93) and preceding energy test
operative_hypotheses: Dimension2, centered stationary isotropic divergence-free Gaussian b with covariance spectrum 1_{|k|<=1}(I-k tensor k/|k|^2) and Fourier measure dk/(2pi)
X0=0, dX=epsilon b(X)dt+sqrt(2)dW, unit xi, fixed finite nonzero epsilon for the counterevidence
Stationary v solves partial_t v-Delta v-epsilon b.grad v=epsilon b.xi, v(0)=0; ultraviolet smoothness and finite Gaussian moments
findings.evidence: Energy testing gives (1/2)d_t E[v^2]+E|grad v|^2=E[epsilon(b.xi)v]. Thus D(T)=(1/2)E(xi.XT)^2=T+(1/2)E v(T)^2+integral E|grad v|^2, not the printed coefficient1. In the actual Gaussian ensemble E(b.xi)^2=1/4. Independent generator expansion gives D(T)=T+epsilon^2*T^2/8+O(T^3); printed RHS gives T+epsilon^2*T^2/4+O(T^3). Exact spectral integrals and70-digit quadrature atT1 give V=.16143777821281106548, G=.02646115042499717043, D2=.10718003953140270317, D2=V/2+G.
findings.core_dependency: Lemma9.1 is the explicit bridge from the parabolic problem to mean squared displacement in Theorem1.1; the wrong coefficient propagates into energy and(99).
alternate_readings_and_counterevidence: v normalization and sqrt2 Brownian coefficient are fixed; page22 independently uses the correct half in an energy test.
Correcting terminal coefficients leaves the leading proxy-gradient term and norm bounds in(98)–(102) of the same order.
No counterexample to T sqrt(log T), the small-epsilon asymptotic statement, or stationary Theorem1.2 is established.
findings.repair: Use terminal coefficient1/2 in(90),(93), the energy definition and all terminal terms of(99). Independently justify the finite-time monotonicity invoked for the all-amplitude lower bound.
findings.impact: Demonstrated false exact core identity and invalid printed derivation; not a demonstrated false final theorem. The finite-time monotonicity claim remains a verification limit, not an additional established defect.

findings.title: Two incorrect forcing signs in equation(97)
operative_hypotheses: Same Gaussian model; L=sqrt(T)>=1, time-independent proxy tilde_phi_L
Residual fixed by a_L(xi+grad tilde_phi_L)=tilde_lambda_L xi+Jgrad tilde_sigma_L+f_L
First-step demonstration uses M>1,epsilon!=0 and independent low/high Fourier shells
findings.evidence: Taking divergence of(50) yields Delta tilde_phi+epsilon b_L.(xi+grad tilde_phi)=div f. Therefore (partial_t-Delta-epsilon b.grad)(v-tilde_phi)=epsilon(b-b_L).xi+epsilon div[tilde_phi(b-b_L)]+div f. The printed last two signs are minus. At L=M, expected conditional variance of the discrepancy given the high shell is epsilon^4 log(M)/(2M^2)>0.
findings.core_dependency: Parabolic comparison equation used to derive the Gronwall error estimate(98).
alternate_readings_and_counterevidence: Residual sign cannot be changed alone because(50) fixes it.
Subsequent energy estimates take norms of forcing terms, so their magnitude and order survive both sign corrections.
findings.repair: Replace the last two forcing signs in(97) by plus signs.
findings.impact: Local formula error; no demonstrated false Gronwall estimate or final theorem.
findings.independent_computation: Exact low-mode covariance and gradient variance in independent_results.json; algebraic proof in report.

findings.title: Missing imaginary unit in the Fourier stream-function coupling
operative_hypotheses: Fourier convention exp(-i k.x), real b and psi, b_L=-Jgrad psi_L, nonzero wavevector within truncated spectral support
findings.evidence: Fpsi_L=i|k|^-2 1_{|k|>=L^-1} Jk.Fb. The printed odd real multiplier violates Hermitian reality. Exact operator-mode check k=(3/5,4/5),psi=cos(k.x), b=Jk sin(k.x) gives bhat+=(2i/5,-3i/10); printed psi coefficients at+/-k are-i/2, corrected coefficients1/2.
findings.core_dependency: Construction of the real coupled Gaussian stream functions and independent shell increments.
alternate_readings_and_counterevidence: The deterministic mode is an operator test, not a Gaussian-ensemble counterexample.
Source(11),(13) and real-valued energy arguments specify the intended real convention; correcting the phase preserves covariance and shell independence.
findings.impact: Local coupling formula error; intended covariance model and downstream estimates are not disproved.
findings.independent_computation: Exact complex rational symbolic check in independent_results.json.

findings.title: Rotations alone do not imply a scalar homogenized matrix
operative_hypotheses: Real2x2 effective matrix; isotropic centered radial Gaussian stream field; covariance of corrector construction under orthogonal coordinate changes
findings.evidence: SO(2) commutant consists of alpha I+beta J; I+J is a nonscalar counterexample to the printed implication. Actual model has psi^Q(x)=det(Q)psi(Qx) equal in law to psi. Q^T a(Qx)Q=I+epsilon psi^Q J. Reflection Q=diag(1,-1) forces beta=0.
findings.core_dependency: Lemma3.2 identifies a scalar effective diffusivity used in main comparisons.
alternate_readings_and_counterevidence: The actual model has the needed reflection/sign symmetry, so the lemma's conclusion is repairable and not false.
The determinant rule is already explicit in source(40),(44),(67); continuum follow-up2404.00709v2 p3 distinguishes scalar-times-rotation.
findings.repair: Add reflection covariance to the rotation argument.
findings.impact: Local missing logical step; no false scalar conclusion or main theorem established.
findings.independent_computation: Exact symbolic rotation commutant check in independent_results.json; full reflection argument in report.

findings.title: Initial-scale exception and overstated uniformity of the proxy moment bound
operative_hypotheses: Page9 constants depend only on epsilon and are bounded for epsilon^2<=1; page15 quantifies every sufficiently large M
Main theorem proof chooses M in a bounded range of sufficiently large constants
findings.evidence: With a=epsilon^2 logM,(77) atL1 requires a<=1 without hypothesis. At firststep tilde_lambda_M=1+a/2, tilde_phi_M=epsilon phi'_1, E(phi'_1)^2=(M^2-1)/4, so ratio tilde_lambda_M^2 Etilde_phi_M^2/(epsilon^2 M^2)=(1+a/2)^2(1-M^-2)/4. This diverges asM->infinity for every fixed nonzero epsilon, refuting a bound uniform over allM>=M0 even if C depends on epsilon. Exact recurrence z_(n+1)=z_n+a+a^2/(4z_n),z0=1 gives zN-(1+Na)=sum a^2/(4z_n). Page14's missing1 yields1<=0 atN0.
findings.core_dependency: Proxy moment and residual estimates in Lemmas6.1,7.1, then Theorems1.1,1.2.
alternate_readings_and_counterevidence: For L>=M,(77) is valid; firststep is valid when a<=1.
A fixed bounded M range with separate initial-step treatment and C_epsilon for largeepsilon avoids the counterexample; main proof uses such bounded M choices.
Statement(59) already includes the correct initial1, and exact recurrence verifies it.
findings.repair: Restrict M to a fixed bounded admissible range, handle initialstep separately, clarify epsilon dependence, and restore initial1 in page14 display.
findings.impact: False auxiliary uniform-range statement and initialization steps, with bounded local repair for the main proof's actual scale choice. No final asymptotic theorem refuted.
findings.independent_computation: Exact first-step symbolic formula and12 rational recurrence cases in independent_results.json; M->infinity implication proved analytically in report, not claimed as another execution.

findings.title: False uniqueness claim about Gaussian finite-range fields
operative_hypotheses: Usual positive finite range of dependence for centered stationary Gaussian fields; optional isotropic divergence-free vector field
findings.evidence: For nonzero nonconstant radial K in C_c^infinity(R2),supported in radiusR, G=K*W has covarianceK*tilde K supported in radius2R. Gaussian fields on separated sets are independent. G is smooth and not white noise; JgradG also gives a smooth isotropic divergence-free finite-range Gaussian field.
findings.core_dependency: Introductory motivation only; no operative proof depends on uniqueness assertion.
alternate_readings_and_counterevidence: Independence at every positive separation would be a different zero-range statement.
Example does not have the paper's selected spectral density and is not a counterexample to its theorems.
findings.repair: Distinguish zero-range independence from finite positive range or remove uniqueness assertion.
findings.independent_computation: Analytic covariance/support proof in report; no code execution needed or claimed.
